threads.body: Passing `None` disables `UploadCompletionHook`'s real path for attaching the generated references to a span. The committed data therefore has no spans, and every report lists these three new span attributes as `(none)`. Exercise the hook with a genuine GenAI operation span and regenerate the scenario data and reports so the changes in `spans.yaml` have reference coverage.

threads.body: `CompletionRefs` in the pinned `opentelemetry-util-genai==1.1b0` also has `tool_definitions_ref`, and `on_completion` schedules that upload when `tool_definitions` is non-empty. This map omits its path, but both the drop handler and `_do_upload` unconditionally look up every scheduled path, so a tool-definition upload raises `KeyError` instead of completing normally. Either make the receipt lookup optional and skip result events for this unmodeled content type, or add the corresponding reference convention and mapping.

This declares an inference client span, but the span wraps only `UploadCompletionHook.on_completion`; no model or GenAI service call occurs. That conflicts with `reference/CONTRIBUTING.md:101-113` and this scenario's README, and it makes the generated report falsely list `opentelemetry-util-genai` as inference support while producing missing-inference-attribute findings. Demonstrate span enrichment in a provider or framework scenario whose span wraps the real operation, and keep this scenario focused on the storage-result event.

This issue also appears on line 189 of the same file.

threads.body: The shared content group does not cover every signal that already records these values. `gen_ai.fetch_response.client` declares system instructions and output messages directly at lines 383 and 389, `gen_ai.create_agent.client` declares system instructions at line 506, and `gen_ai.invoke_workflow.internal` declares input and output messages at lines 665 and 667. Those signals therefore cannot provide the new external reference for content they support. Add the matching `_ref` attributes to those signal definitions, or explicitly narrow the reference contract to the signals covered by this group.

replies.body: Expanded: consumers must not parse the URI to derive provider, format or storage outcome, and need separate access to resolve it.

Semantic conventions are not authoritative for consumers of telemetry, only for producers controlled by otel, plus it does not seem to be necessary to put any expectations on consumers.

An example of how it's used in the wild https://docs.cloud.google.com/stackdriver/docs/instrumentation/collect-view-multimodal-prompts-responses- the upload behavior and consumption are controlled by the same platform; credentials, destination, and consumption etc are all controlled by the same entity.  It's easy to imagine that any other company can have a distro that uploads using their custom code to a storage of their preference with access model aligned with telemetry producer. 

I think `opaque` can't come with MUST and I don't think it's helpful at all. Why do we care in semantic conventions about it?
Agreed. The consumer wording is removed from all four `_ref` attributes in the latest push, using your suggestion on the storage outcome sentence.

threads.body: The PR description promises that enabling inline capture alone will not enable uploads or reference attributes. `SHOULD` allows exceptions to that separation, so it does not enforce the stated guarantee for these potentially sensitive values. replies.body: Keeping `SHOULD`. The maintainer review in https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/pull/490#discussion_r4262102317 asked for it, so a combined capture mode flag or an instrumentation that only supports external storage stays conforming. The PR description promised the stricter rule, and I updated it to match.
